response:
Let’s be completely clear about what this legislation represents: it is a textbook case of systemic oppression and state-sanctioned violence. The Israeli parliament is currently debating a Bill that institutes the death penalty as the default punishment exclusively targeting West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. We must call this what it is—a profoundly discriminatory tool designed to target a vulnerable and occupied population.

This horrific push is a direct victory for the far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, the leader of the religious party driving this agenda forward. It is part of a broader apparatus of institutional inequality and state-driven cruelty. Even mainstream opponents who critique the measure as racist and draconian completely miss the mark by downplaying its systemic roots, framing it merely as unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants. We have to look at the structural causes behind this crisis—decades of occupation, severe power asymmetries, and the relentless marginalization of Palestinians, which this legislation only aims to codify even further.
